\section[\texorpdfstring{\bn{বাজি} \bn{ধরা} (bāji dhôrā)}{বাজি ধরা (bāji dhôrā)}]{\bn{বাজি} \bn{ধরা} (bāji dhôrā) — to bet; to place a wager}

\label{lesson:BN-C534-baji-dhora}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Bengali for to slip away, then the Bengali for a lottery.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \bn{বাজি} \bn{ধরা}}
\textbf{\bn{বাজি} \bn{ধরা}} — \emph{bāji dhôrā} — \textquotedblleft{}to bet; to place a wager\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\bn{বাজি} \bn{ধরলে} \bn{তুমি} \bn{সব} \bn{টাকা} \bn{হারাবে।}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Bāji dhôrle tumi sôb ṭākā hārābe.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
If you bet, you'll lose all your money.
\end{quote}

Past (he/she …): \bn{তিনি} \bn{ম্যাচে} \bn{বাজি} \bn{ধরলেন}, \emph{tini mæche bāji dhôrlen}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\bn{বাজি} \bn{ধরা}} (\emph{bāji dhôrā}) joins \bn{বাজি}, \textquotedblleft{}a bet\textquotedblright{}, usually traced to Persian \emph{bāzī}, \textquotedblleft{}play, a game\textquotedblright{}, to \bn{ধরা}, \textquotedblleft{}to hold\textquotedblright{}: to hold to a wager.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for saying what happens if.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{bāji dhôrā}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{bāji dhôrā}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{Bāji dhôrle tumi sôb ṭākā hārābe.} — If you bet, you'll lose all your money.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Bengali for to slip away, then the Bengali for a lottery, then say \emph{bāji dhôrā} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \bn{বাজি} \bn{ধরা} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To bet; to place a wager\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\bn{জুয়া} (juyā)}{জুয়া (juyā)}]{\bn{জুয়া} (juyā) — gambling}

\label{lesson:BN-C534-juya}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Bengali for a lottery, then the Bengali for to bet.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \bn{জুয়া}}
\textbf{\bn{জুয়া}} — \emph{juyā} — \textquotedblleft{}gambling\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\bn{জুয়ায়} \bn{লোকটা} \bn{তার} \bn{সঞ্চয়} \bn{হারাল।}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Juyāy lokṭā tār sôñchôy hārālô.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The man lost his savings gambling.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\bn{জুয়া}} (\emph{juyā}) is a tadbhava: CDIAL lists Bengali \emph{juyā}, \textquotedblleft{}gambling\textquotedblright{}, under Sanskrit \emph{dyūta} (CDIAL 6608).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for saying what happens if.

\section[\texorpdfstring{\bn{টস} (ṭôs)}{টস (ṭôs)}]{\bn{টস} (ṭôs) — a coin toss}

\label{lesson:BN-C534-tos}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Bengali for to bet, then the Bengali for gambling.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \bn{টস}}
\textbf{\bn{টস}} — \emph{ṭôs} — \textquotedblleft{}a coin toss\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\bn{টস} \bn{জিতলে} \bn{অধিনায়ক} \bn{আগে} \bn{ব্যাট} \bn{করবে।}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Ṭôs jitle ôdhināyôk āge bæṭ kôrbe.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
If the captain wins the toss, she will bat first.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\bn{টস}} (\emph{ṭôs}) is borrowed from English \emph{toss}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for saying what happens if.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ṭôs}, once more

  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Bengali for to bet, then the Bengali for gambling, then say \emph{ṭôs} again
\end{itemize}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\bn{শুভ} (shubhô)}{শুভ (shubhô)}]{\bn{শুভ} (shubhô) — auspicious; good}

\label{lesson:BN-C534-shubho}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Bengali for gambling, then the Bengali for a coin toss.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \bn{শুভ}}
\textbf{\bn{শুভ}} — \emph{shubhô} — \textquotedblleft{}auspicious; good\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\bn{বিয়ের} \bn{জন্য} \bn{এটা} \bn{একটা} \bn{শুভ} \bn{দিন।}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Biyer jônyô eṭā ekṭā shubhô din.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
This is an auspicious day for a wedding.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\bn{শুভ}} (\emph{shubhô}) is a tatsama, Sanskrit \emph{śubha}, \textquotedblleft{}bright, beautiful, auspicious\textquotedblright{} (Monier-Williams).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for saying what happens if.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\bn{ফলা} (phôlā)}{ফলা (phôlā)}]{\bn{ফলা} (phôlā) — to come true; to bear fruit}

\label{lesson:BN-C534-phola-bear-fruit}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Bengali for a coin toss, then the Bengali for auspicious.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \bn{ফলা}}
\textbf{\bn{ফলা}} — \emph{phôlā} — \textquotedblleft{}to come true; to bear fruit\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\bn{জ্যোতিষীর} \bn{কথা} \bn{ফলল।}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Jyotishīr kôthā phôllô.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The astrologer's words came true.
\end{quote}

Past (he/she …): \bn{সেই} \bn{গাছে} \bn{আম} \bn{ফলল}, \emph{sei gāchhe ām phôllô}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\bn{ফলা}} (\emph{phôlā}) is a tadbhava: CDIAL lists Bengali \emph{phalā}, \textquotedblleft{}to bear fruit\textquotedblright{}, under Sanskrit \emph{phalati} (CDIAL 9057); a prediction that comes true has borne fruit.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for saying what happens if.
\end{grammarlens}
